'''''Ligustrum ovalifolium''''', also known as '''Korean privet''',<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|title=English Names for Korean Native Plants|publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]]|year=2015|isbn=978-89-97450-98-5|location=Pocheon|pages=518|access-date=19 December 2016|via=[[Korea Forest Service]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|archivedate=25 May 2017}}</ref> '''California privet''', '''garden privet''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> and '''oval-leaved privet''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the olive [[family (botany)|family]] Oleaceae.<ref name="bu">[http://www.bellarmine.edu/faculty/drobinson/CaliforniaPrivet.htm Bellarmine University: ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' (California Privet)]</ref> The species is [[native plant|native]] to [[Japan]] and [[Korea]].<ref name="bu"/> 

==Description==
''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' is a dense, fast-growing, [[deciduous]] ([[evergreen]]/semi-evergreen in warm winter areas) shrub or small tree. It grows to {{convert|10|-|15|ft|m}} tall and wide.<ref name="mbg">[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=c323 Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder: ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' (California privet)]</ref> Its thick, fleshy leaf is green on the top, and greenish-yellow on the underside.<ref name="bu"/>

It flowers in midsummer, the abundant white blooms producing a unique pungent fragrance, unpleasant to some.<ref name="bu"/> They are borne in [[inflorescence|panicles]]. They have four curled-back [[petals]] and two high [[stamens]] with yellow or red anthers, between which is the low [[gynoecium|pistil]]; the petals and stamens fall off after the flower is fertilized, leaving the pistil in the [[sepal|calyx tube]]. Flowering starts after 330 [[growing degree day]]s.{{cn|date=November 2019}}

The fruits, borne in clusters, are small purple to black [[drupes]], poisonous for humans but readily eaten by many birds.<ref name="bu"/> In favorable growing conditions, individual shrubs may produce thousands of [[fruit]]s.<ref>Hasskarl, Justus Carl. 1844. Catalogus Plantarum in Horto Botanico Bogoriensi Cultarum Alter 119.</ref>

==Uses==
''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' is used as a food plant by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species including [[common emerald]], [[common marbled carpet]], [[copper underwing]], [[the engrailed]], [[mottled beauty]], [[scalloped hazel]], [[small angle shades]], [[V-pug|the V-pug]] and [[willow beauty]].<ref name="mbg"/>

All parts of plant are poisonous if ingested by humans.<ref>[http://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/1725/#b PlantFiles: ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'']</ref> 

===Cultivation===
The species is widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] in many countries, as a [[shrub]], and grouped for an informal or formal [[hedge]].<ref name="mbg"/><ref name="bu"/> Privets need to be trimmed several times during a growing season, in order to maintain a formal hedge shape. Regularly trimmed plants do not produce flowers or fruit.

''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' is the most common [[hedge|hedging]] plant species in cultivation in the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Agate|first=Elizabeth|title=Hedging: a practical handbook|year=1998|publisher=British Trust for Conservation Volunteers|isbn=0946752176|pages=125}}</ref>

Several [[cultivars]] are used in gardens and for hedging, including ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' 'Aureum', the golden privet, with oval, rich yellow leaves with green centers.<ref>[http://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/54272/ PlantFiles: Detailed information on Golden Privet—''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' 'Aureum']</ref> In the [[UK]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' 'Aureum'|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1158|accessdate=21 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 60 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 22 March 2018}}</ref> With ''[[Ligustrum obtusifolium]]'' it is a parent of the hybrid [[Ligustrum × ibolium|''Ligustrum'' × ''ibolium'']].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=244818 |title=''Ligustrum'' × ''ibolium'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Plant Finder |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=6 December 2020 }}</ref>

''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' 'Vicaryi', a yellow-leaved shrub, was once thought to be a hybrid between ''L. ovalifolium'' 'Aureum' and ''[[Ligustrum vulgare]]'', for which the name ''Ligustrum'' × ''vicaryi'' was published. Studies of both [[chloroplast]] and [[Cell nucleus|nuclear]] [[DNA]] showed that ''L. vulgare'' was not involved in its parentage, both of its parents being ''L. ovalifolium''. Accordingly, it was given a cultivar name. Its year-round yellow leaves and white flowers in midsummer make it an attractive hedging plant or ornamental shrub.<ref name=Edwa16>{{Citation |mode=cs1 |last1=Edwards |first1=Dawn |date=2016 |title=The origin of ''Ligustrum'' × ''vicaryi'' |journal=The Plantsman |series=New Series |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=160–161 }}</ref>

==Naturalized—invasive species==
The species is reportedly naturalized in [[France]], [[Spain]], [[Italy]], the [[Balearic Islands]], [[Saint Helena]], [[Réunion]], [[Chiapas]] (México), [[Costa Rica]], [[Guatemala]], [[Honduras]], the [[Juan Fernandez Islands]], [[Ontario]], and in the [[United States]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=354221 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'']</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Ligustrum%20ovalifolium.png Biota of North America Program, ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'']</ref>

''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' has also been listed as an [[invasive species]] in areas of the United States, including: [[California]], [[Hawaii]], [[Washington (state)|Washington state]], [[Texas]], [[Missouri]], [[Alabama]], and many of the Mid-Atlantic and [[Northeastern United States|Northeastern states]].<ref>[http://www.invasiveplantatlas.org/subject.html?sub=11561 Invasive Plant Atlas of the United States: ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' (California privet)]</ref><ref>{{cite book |url=http://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/midatlantic.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061007092003/http://www.nps.gov/plants/alien/pubs/midatlantic/midatlantic.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 7, 2006 | title=Plant Invaders of Mid-Atlantic Natural Areas, 4th Edition |last1=Swearingen |first1=Jil |last2=Reshetiloff |first2=K. |last3=Slattery |first3=B |last4=Zwicker |first4=S. | year=2010 |publisher=National Park Service and U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service |page=71}}</ref><ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Ligustrum+ovalifolium CalFlora Database: ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'']</ref> 46 states have it listed on their [[noxious weed]] lists.<ref>[http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=LIOV USDA: U.S. Weed Information for ''Ligustrum ovalifolium'' (California privet)]</ref>

==Etymology==
''Ligustrum'' means "binder". It was named by [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]] and Virgil.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  p 237</ref> The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''ovalifolium'' means "oval-leaved".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>
